reference: Contract cases use Bash type/help behavior and the pinned loadable's published synopsis/help strings as the documented contract; expected bytes are written independently from those strings and never copied from a candidate run. wipefs is a util-linux command, not a GNU utility, and no matching external oracle is available here, so no parity comparison is claimed. Signature inspection and erasure are deferred under the requested safety limits.
coverage: Bash reports wipefs as a builtin with the executable search path disabled by the runner.
Bash help registration and the loadable's published synopsis are checked.
The command's own --help output is checked against its published help text.
Future safe inspection, dry-run, and erase behavior is specified as deferred work with independent reference requirements.
exclusions: No wipefs operation is executed: even regular-file signature erasure is a destructive loadable operation forbidden by this task.
No parity case is claimed because wipefs is from util-linux rather than GNU and no external wipefs oracle is installed in this environment.
No block device, loop device, mount, or real system path is used.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves the loadable as a builtin when candidate execution uses an empty PATH.
Verify Bash has registered help for wipefs; the marker makes the expected output independent of help formatting.
Check Bash's short-help form against the usage synopsis declared in the builtin table entry.
Check wipefs --help prints the documented mode descriptions and signature-family scope without opening a target.
cases.stdout:
Detect or wipe filesystem / swap signatures.

    wipefs device       list detected signatures (offset, type)
    wipefs -a device    erase all detected signatures
    wipefs -n device    dry-run: show what -a would erase

Recognises swap, ext, xfs, btrfs, ntfs, vfat and iso9660 magics.

cases.purpose: Qualify default listing and -n behavior over synthetic signatures, no-signature inputs, and repeated operands while proving reads do not change fixture bytes.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable fixture environment with a separately installed util-linux wipefs reference (or independently specified expected rows) and a small regular-file corpus encoded from filesystem-format references. Compare statuses and exact signature rows for empty, unmatched, and supported signatures; verify default and -n leave all bytes unchanged. No operation ran in this suite.

cases.purpose: Qualify -a byte changes, including multiple signatures and preservation of unrelated fixture data.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed private-image mock that confines all writes to throwaway regular-file images, plus independently encoded signature vectors and an independent util-linux/reference-byte oracle. Verify -a clears only specified magic bytes, preserves neighboring data, and compare repeated/no-match behavior; separately verify -n preserves the image. The destructive operation is not run here.
